rules.providerNativeEquivalence: Different provider-native mechanisms are allowed only where equivalence is explicitly named; evidence must still prove the same user-visible fact and may not substitute a dashboard label for an executed witness.
rules.armSpecificConstraints: A gate scoped to one arm constrains that arm's implementation and is reported separately from the symmetric product-completeness result.

gates.requirement: Authenticated owner identity is derived by the server and cannot be selected by client input.
The authenticated owner can create a conversation.
The authenticated owner can rename a conversation.
The authenticated owner can list only their conversations.
The authenticated owner can select one of their conversations.
The authenticated owner can delete a conversation.
Conversation messages have an authoritative stable order.
Sending one prompt creates one user message and one assistant placeholder.
A second client observes at least three distinct authoritative intermediate commits before terminal completion.
The source emits 16 numbered UTF-8 chunks over at least 800 ms.
Cancellation reaches the upstream reader, records cancelled settlement, and prevents every late commit.
Retry reuses one attempt identity and duplicates neither user nor assistant message.
Complete, failed, cancelled, timed-out, and ambiguous settlements remain distinct.
The witness proves 1 MiB total, 64 KiB buffered, 30 s wall, 5 s idle, and 10 authoritative commits/second ceilings.
The implementation applies backpressure instead of unbounded eager reads.
Failure diagnostics are secret-safe and identify operation, source locus, expected shape, safe received summary, and repair guidance.
A second authenticated principal cannot read the first principal's conversations or messages.
A second authenticated principal cannot subscribe to the first principal's data.
A second authenticated principal cannot rename the first principal's conversation.
A second authenticated principal cannot delete the first principal's conversation.
A second authenticated principal cannot patch stream progress for the first principal.
Reconnect produces an authoritative provider-native push snapshot while fallback is disabled.
An exact public HTTPS origin serves the actual React application.
The receipt proves a newly isolated target and exact account, target, deployment, and origin identity.
The deployed code and artifacts are retained with immutable content identities.
Schema, client, and runtime compatibility are checked before activation using the arm's native mechanism.
Required secrets/configuration are declared and proven present without exposing values.
Structured build/runtime logs and authenticated inspection are retained through provider-native CLI, dashboard, or receipt evidence.
A compatible next release can be activated and rolled back without data rewind.
Backup is read back and an isolated destroy, restore, verify, and activate drill succeeds.
Stale target, wrong account/origin, and preview/production confusion fail closed.
Cleanup retires every resource created by the run and no resource outside the run.
The shared product surface passes the untimed Expo iOS Simulator compatibility check.

One installed schema drives validators/types; the required owned CRUD, unique lookup, and keyset page generators are used; generated references are the only app-data call surface; trusted fields are server-derived; and no forbidden handwritten substitute satisfies the gate.
One authored command from the application root builds, preflights, deploys, and activates the hosted application.
Every Snapback package resolves from the public npm registry with exact integrity and no workspace, path, Git, tarball, sibling, or repository-local runtime dependency.
